body.p: Dyooa. Dyooa lives with his grandmother and his brother near the river overgrown with bushes. Somehow they live. They get fish, they kill partridges. One day they had no prey at all, they ate all the dried fish they had in the tent. There was a copper pot with caviar left with them. What can one do? Suddenly, Dyooa said to the grandmother and to his brother: "I got sick, I got very sick, I'll probably die. When I die, bury me on the way to the river, make me a coffin, put the pot of caviar under the coffin." At some point, Dyooa died. The grandmother and his brother are crying, they feel sorry for Dyooa. What can one do? They buried him, they made a coffin, they put a copper pot with caviar there. Dyooa's brother goes to see his net every day, for some reason he has no prey at all. One day, passing by the coffin of his late Dyooa, he saw fish bones. The next day, he again walked near his brother's coffin, he saw that there were a lot of fish bones. He thought: "Someone is sending fish to my deceased". He went home. Suddenly, someone behind him laughs softly: "Ha-ha." He looked around, what is it? Dyooa laughs looking out of his coffin, and caviar pours out of his mouth through his teeth and through the opening of the coffin. The next day, Dyooa's brother again walked along the coffin, again heard a quiet laugh, looked around and again saw as follows - the late Dea laughs: "Ha-ha." Again, caviar pours through his teeth and through the opening of his coffin. He came home and said to the grandmother: "When I go along Dyooa's coffin, my brother, it seems to me, always laughs, caviar falls through his teeth and through the opening of his coffin.". It seems, he did not die." The next day, Dyooa's brother again walked along the coffin, again he heard laugh. He looked around and cried: "Dyooa, the bear is coming, the bear is coming." The deceased ran out of the coffin screaming and crying like this: "Where is the bear, where?". It turns out that he really did not die, he deceived his grandmother and brother because of the caviar.
